title: Cancer: When Cells Divide Wrong
hook: Cancer is cell division gone unchecked — a cell ignores the body's stop signals, multiplies relentlessly, and crowds out healthy tissue.
key_points: Healthy cells divide on cue and stop when told; cancer cells ignore those controls.
Cancer starts with mutations in genes that govern when a cell grows, rests, or dies.
Uncontrolled division builds a tumor, and some cells can break away and spread (metastasis).
Because it begins in our own cells, cancer is many diseases rather than a single one.
content_html: Every day your body makes billions of new cells through controlled division, and just as importantly, it knows when to stop. Cancer is what happens when that control breaks down. A cell stops listening to the signals that tell it to pause, repair, or die, and instead keeps dividing — building a mass of cells that serves no purpose and steals resources from the tissue around it.
extra_html: As the NIH National Cancer Institute explains, cancer almost always traces back to mutations in the genes that govern the cell cycle — the genes that say "grow," "stop," or "self-destruct." When enough of these controls fail, a single rogue cell divides into a tumor, and in many cancers some of those cells learn to break away, travel through the blood or lymph, and seed new growths elsewhere, a process called metastasis. Because cancer arises from our own cells rather than an outside invader, it is really a family of more than a hundred diseases, each defined by which cells went wrong and which genetic controls failed — which is why no single cure fits them all.

related.title: Mitosis: One Cell Becomes Two
related.hook: Right now, millions of your cells are copying their DNA and splitting in two — the everyday process that lets you grow, heal, and replace worn-out cells.

related.title: What Is DNA?
related.hook: A four-letter chemical code, coiled into a double helix, carries the full instruction manual for building and running a living thing.

flashcards.prompt: At its core, what is cancer?
flashcards.back_html: Cancer is uncontrolled cell division. A cell stops obeying the body's signals to stop growing or to die, and instead multiplies relentlessly, crowding out healthy tissue.

flashcards.prompt: What underlying change first turns a normal cell cancerous?

choices.text: Mutations in genes that control growth, rest, and cell death
An infection that replaces all the cell's DNA with viral DNA
The cell running completely out of water

flashcards.explanation_html: Cancer begins with mutations in the genes that normally regulate when a cell divides, pauses, or self-destructs. When those controls fail, the cell divides without restraint.

choices.text: When cancer cells break away and spread to other parts of the body
When a tumor shrinks and disappears on its own
The normal process of a cell repairing its DNA

flashcards.explanation_html: Metastasis is the spread of cancer cells from where they started to distant sites in the body. It is what makes many cancers especially dangerous to treat.
